17:32 Local Time, 08:02 GMT, 13:32 IST: Bangladesh find themselves in a very strong position after the opening day of the Test. Cummins won the toss and elected to bat but things didn't go the way he would have hoped. Both Head and Weatherald got off to starts but couldn't capitalise. There was assistance with the new ball for the Bangladeshi seamers and they were on the money. The fact all the ten wickets were bagged by their seamers tells you the story. They picked up four wickets in the first session. There was a promising period for the hosts post lunch as the duo of Smith and Carey batted with composure and assurance. But just after drinks, there was another collapse and that pushed the hosts completely on the back foot. Apart from Smith who made the most of his opportunity (dropped on 2) and went on to score a brilliant 71, the others faltered. He didn't have enough support and Australia got bowled out for 198. Hasan Mahmud stole the limelight and recorded his career-best figures of 6/55.

In response, both Starc and Hazlewood weren't at their best with the new ball and that allowed the Bangladeshi openers to lay a platform. Shadman Islam eventually fell to Starc but he still did a decent job. Mominul came in and was solid as a rock while the young Tanzid who is only playing his second Test showed a lot of reliability too. The duo have stitched an unbeaten 60-run stand and have largely been unfazed. Although there's movement on offer if you land it in the right areas, the surface is on the slower side and that actually suits Bangladesh's style of play. The visitors only trail by 102 runs and their batting lineup is well-equipped for these conditions. Australia are playing the chasing game but we all know they are a champion side and they might well surprise us tomorrow morning. Join us on Day 2 to catch all the action. Goodbye for now...
